title: Reverse characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $V$ a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] of dimension $n=\dim_KV$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], $F:V\to V$ a $K$-linear endomorphism, and $T$ an indeterminate, with polynomial ring $K[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. The reverse characteristic polynomial of $F$ is

$$
 \det(1-TF\mid V)\in K[T],
$$

the determinant [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant] of the $K[T]$-linear endomorphism $1-T\,(F\otimes1)$ of the free $K[T]$-module $V\otimes_KK[T]$ of rank $n$. Concretely, if $A\in M_n(K)$ is the matrix of $F$ in a basis of $V$, it is $\det(I_n-TA)$, and this does not depend on the basis. It is the reverse $T^n\chi_F(1/T)$ of the characteristic polynomial $\chi_F(T)=\det(T-F\mid V)$.
